clue.text: Painter with bone in a crush

indicators.note: the bone sits in the crush, so one word's letters are placed inside the other's

parts.note: a pash is old schoolgirl slang for a crush or infatuation
the ulna is a bone of the forearm

explanation.surface: An artist holding a bone gets caught up in a jostling crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like a crowd, but here it is a passing infatuation, PASH. Paul Nash was an English landscape and war painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Nash was a twentieth-century British artist famed for war landscapes, so a painter by profession.

clue.text: See 22
Glass in front of car

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel and the leading part of a vehicle, an odd pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimming toast glass is called by this name, and so is the protective bar fixed across a car's nose.

clue.text: Farewell to revolutionary meeting his end somewhere in South America

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: the end of the revolutionary's name is its final letter, taken here

parts.note: his points back to the revolutionary just named, so it stands for the same name
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A goodbye to a revolutionary who dies somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his end' is the last letter of CHE, an E, not a death.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: 12's friend's holding is far off

indicators.note: the friend holds the other letters inside it, a container

parts.note: pal is a friend; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: off means the letters of is far are set awry and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wagner's friend, it seems, keeps a holding that is far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges IS FAR into ARSIFA, held inside PAL. 12 is WAGNER, so the definition is Wagner's opera and hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsifal is Wagner's last opera and its holy-fool hero, so something belonging to the composer.

clue.text: 12's minstrel finds sixpence around his residence

indicators.note: the old coin goes around the residence, a container

parts.note: a tanner was slang for the pre-decimal British sixpence coin
his refers to the German composer, whose word for house is Haus

explanation.surface: Wagner's minstrel finds an old coin lying round his house.
explanation.walkthrough: A TANNER is old British slang for a sixpence; 'his' points to Wagner, a German, so his residence is HAUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannhauser is the minnesinger, a medieval minstrel, who gives Wagner's opera its title.

clue.text: 12's girl is getting on with drug

parts.note: someone getting on in years is old
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Wagner's girl is ageing and on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde, so the composer's leading lady.

clue.text: Inlet for compassion, keeping English from 12's place

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea

indicators.note: compassion keeps the English letter inside it, a container

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion

explanation.surface: An inlet offered for pity, keeping the English away from Wagner's town.
explanation.walkthrough: RUTH, the root of 'ruthless', means compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayreuth is the Bavarian town where Wagner built his festival theatre, so his home ground.

clue.text: Tennis player, a good one, entertaining a fool

indicators.note: the first pieces play host to the fool, holding it inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A tennis player, and a good one, playing host to a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi was an American tennis champion with eight Grand Slam titles.

clue.text: To be a woodwind player is a poisonous job

explanation.surface: Playing a wind instrument is said to be a toxic occupation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, it is what a woodwind player does: blow a pipe. As one, it is the tube that shoots poisoned darts.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing a pipe is literally playing woodwind, and the hunting tube of that name fires poisoned darts.

clue.text: How surprised can one be changing right to left in jest?

indicators.note: right and left are R and L, so the clue swaps one for the other

parts.note: a pleasantry is a joke or jest

explanation.surface: A question about how much a person can be surprised by switching sides in a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the stock phrase 'pleasantly surprised'.
explanation.definitionFit: One can be pleasantly surprised, so the adverb answers the question of manner.

clue.text: Jester to new queen, a fellow of note

parts.note: a wag is a joker or jester
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A court jester to a newly crowned queen turns out to be a notable fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' is a pun: a famous fellow, and one of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was a celebrated composer, a man of note in both the famous and the musical sense.

clue.text: Conductors in a body after some dinner, missing ten Titians

indicators.note: the trimmed painter comes after the piece of dinner
some of the word dinner means just part of it, its final letters
missing means the ten is dropped from the painter's name

parts.note: Titian's family name was Vecellio, here made plural
IO looks like the figure 10, so it can stand for ten

explanation.surface: Musical conductors relax after dinner, short of ten Titian paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian was Tiziano Vecellio; losing IO (10) from VECELLIOS leaves VECELLS. 'Conductors' are not of orchestras but of nerve impulses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve cells conduct electrical impulses through the body, so they are bodily conductors.

clue.text: It's invisible below lightly cooked bit of dinner

parts.note: inf. abbreviates Latin infra, below, as in references
rare meat is lightly cooked

indicators.note: a bit of dinner is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Something unseen lies under a lightly cooked portion of the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared radiation lies beyond the red end of the spectrum, outside human vision.

clue.text: 16's was 12's gift from Portia

explanation.surface: The dwarf's treasure became the composer's, as did Portia's present.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nibelung's ring gives its name to Wagner's Ring cycle; in The Merchant of Venice Portia gives Bassanio a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's four-opera cycle is named after the Nibelung's golden band, and Portia gives a band to Bassanio.

clue.text: Dwarf from Ulster, live, takes breather

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
to be is to live or exist
a lung is the organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: A dwarf from Northern Ireland, very much alive, pauses for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest; it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nibelungs are the dwarf race of Germanic legend, such as Alberich in Wagner's Ring.

clue.text: Hard to find English not recorded outside America

indicators.note: the unrecorded word goes outside America, holding it

parts.note: a live broadcast is not recorded
US is America

explanation.surface: Something hard to track down: English, not recorded, beyond America.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elusive evades capture or discovery, so it is hard to find.

clue.text: 12's rider, boy or girl, at part of Mass

parts.note: Val is short for Valentine or Valerie, so a name for either sex
the Kyrie is an opening section of the Mass

explanation.surface: Wagner's horseman, a boy or girl, attending part of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Valkyries ride through the air in Wagner's Die Walkure, so the composer's riders.

clue.text: 12's to die? Setter is having name put in new register

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: the name is put into the rearranged word
new signals the letters of register are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether to die after a name is added to a fresh register.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's opera is Die Meistersinger, so 'to die?' is completed by the answer. 'new' rearranges REGISTER, into which N is 'put in' to give TERSINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Die Meistersinger von Nurnberg is a Wagner opera, so the answer follows 'Die' in his title.

clue.text: Silly symbol nearly meet

parts.note: a silly person is an ass

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the word for symbol is lost

parts.note: an emblem is a symbol

explanation.surface: A silly symbol almost manages to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather or come together, which is to meet.

clue.text: See 21
Stoker and railway both turned to stone

indicators.note: both says each of the two words is turned back to front

parts.note: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula
an el is an elevated railway in the US

explanation.surface: A stoker and a railway both turned to stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoker' looks like a boiler-man near a railway; it is Bram Stoker. BRAM turns to MARB, EL to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble is a hard crystalline stone used for sculpture and building.

clue.text: Location of curl in morally extreme girl of conventional tastes

definitions.text: Location of curl in morally extreme girl

explanation.surface: Where a little girl's curl lay and a person of safe tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme girl 'had a little curl right in the middle of her forehead': when good, very good, when bad, horrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlebrow describes taste that is conventional, neither highbrow nor lowbrow; the curl lay mid-forehead.

clue.text: Potential duel is near being resolved

indicators.note: resolved here means broken up and worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A possible duel is close to being settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Potential that has not yet come to fruition is unrealised, as yet unfulfilled.

clue.text: Foreign country picks up the bill

explanation.surface: Abroad someone settles the account.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a land or nation, and the verb for settling up a bill.

clue.text: See 10
Charming falcon

explanation.surface: A charming falcon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' is not 'delightful' but casting charms, as Arthur's wizard did.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian wizard works charms, and a small falcon shares his name.

clue.text: Summon back round piece of film from great circle

indicators.note: the reversed summons goes round the film piece, a container
back means the word for summon is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to cite is to summon to court
a clip is a short extract from a film

explanation.surface: A summons is recalled over a piece of film taken from a great circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summon' is in the legal sense, calling someone to court; 'back' and 'round' are the indicators, and 'from' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecliptic is the great circle on the celestial sphere traced by the sun's yearly path.
